description: This donut chart, from the paper “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” visually represents the distribution of data across two distinct categorical dimensions: “(Outer)” which corresponds to standard deviation values (Std: 0.0, Std: 0.47, Std: 0.82, Std: 0.94), and “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” which corresponds to maximum ambiguity levels (Max: 1, Max: 2, Max: 3). The chart is composed of four outer segments and three inner segments, with the outer segments colored in progressively lighter shades of blue and the inner segments in progressively lighter shades of blue as well. The outer ring, representing standard deviation, is divided into four segments with the following approximate proportions: the darkest blue segment (Std: 0.0) accounts for 49.0%, the next segment (Std: 0.47) is 47.7%, the next (Std: 0.82) is 7.0%, and the lightest blue segment (Std: 0.94) is 5.0%. The inner ring, representing maximum ambiguity, is divided into three segments: the darkest blue segment (Max: 1) is 38.0%, the middle blue segment (Max: 2) is 39.0%, and the lightest blue segment (Max: 3) is 14.2%. The chart includes a legend on the right side that clearly maps the color shades to their respective categories, and percentage values are displayed directly within each segment for easy reference. The segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size from left to right in the outer ring, and similarly for the inner ring.
